title: What the decision actually authorized
question: What changed between the request and the final decision?
finding: Eight comparisons distinguish final enactments, contract ceilings, an amended permit and a proposal still in committee.
how: Read the underlying fiscal analysis or signed decision alongside contemporaneous filing entries. The housing comparison uses the subject rather than an exact Board-file key.
limits: A payment is compensation reported by a lobbyist for a client across the filing period. The reports do not allocate it to a vote, official or contract. Congressional lobbying on behalf of the City is a separate system. Public testimony and specified bargaining with the City have reporting exemptions. An absent contact does not establish that a party took no position. The membership and client-name screen can miss coalitions named only for a campaign or a law firm.

rows.review: The Board disapproved the March 2023 planning approval. The July findings address industrial land and transportation policy. The hearing and disposition have different file numbers.
The Board disapproved the original permit and granted a new conditional authorization for the same project. Its added condition limits parcel delivery use.

The adopted $189 million ceiling includes parking taxes the operator remits. The $9 million increase added two Port facilities. The monthly management fee increased $492. Four firms competed for the two original contracts.

SFO selected the highest-scoring responsive firm through a request for proposals. The analyst found a month outside the three-year term in the budget. The adopted ceiling was $20.1 million, $600,000 below the proposal.

The 2021 amendment exercised a five-year option. The analyst recommended reducing the proposed ceiling by $4,026,423 to $308,271,023. The Board adopted that lower ceiling. Pandemic service demand affected the budget.
IATSE Local 119 reported seeking passage. The Board adopted ordinance 10-16. Its text defines the covered broadcast work and the awarding and enforcement responsibilities.

rows.topic: Affordable housing and the project labor agreement
rows.review: The Building and Construction Trades Council reported asking for a housing pilot. The Carpenters reported seeking delay on project labor agreements for housing. These entries identify the subject without stating this file number. The proposed 2024 ordinance would negotiate coverage for additional housing projects, revise when the $5 million subcontractor exemption ends, and extend the agreement to 2050. The proposal remains in committee.
The Building and Construction Trades Council reported requesting an amendment. The proposed reduced transfer rates were filed in October 2026. There is no enactment number for this file.
